transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-14
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sam Torres (PioneerHealth CISO), Leah Park (Pioneer DevOps), Dr. Omar Haddad (Head of AI)

Summary (auto): Weekly governance/pilot sync — focused on SSO, audit logs, data retention, and SOC2 artifacts.

00:00 Jordan: uh hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood, i'll hand over to priya for the quick tech recap and then we can jump into the items on the security checklist.
00:18 Priya: yeah thanks jordan. quick recap — we saw the pilot traffic for the last 72 hours, median generation latency around 220ms on the hosted route, p95 anywhere 380 to 420 depending on token length. there was one backend retry on thursday that we tracked — looked like a thin tail queueing event.
00:45 Sam: sorry to interrupt, can you repeat the p95 numbers? i want to make sure our SLA comparisons are apples-to-apples.
00:52 Priya: sure, median ~220 ms, p95 roughly 380 to 420 ms. caveat: we were on the default batch config; if we tighten for latency there's some cost tradeoffs.
01:10 Jordan: yeah exactly — cost versus latency tradeoff is something we'll document. today the governance topics are the priority: sso, audit logs, retention, soc2 evidence.
01:24 Leah: quick note on SSO — our test IdP is ready, we want to do SAML test-bindings and a short smoke test. is that something that needs the redwood private plane or can it be done against hosted?
01:38 Priya: you can do SAML against hosted. we support both SAML and oidc, but the SAML metadata flow needs one-time configuration in the console. small gotcha — the redirect URIs in the console are strict.
01:52 Leah: got it. can we get a checklist? we tried earlier and got a 400 during the assertion exchange, i think our nameid format was different.
02:05 Jordan: we'll send a SAML step-by-step. priya, can you note the name id / format guidance?
02:09 Priya: yeah, we prefer transient nameid or hashed epid, um, sorry hashed name, i guess. sometimes the system shows 'Redwood Dedicated' as a display name in the console and that gets confusing, so watch for that.
02:25 Sam: on audit logs — we need to map to our SIEM. what fields are in your audit events? we need request_id, user_id, timestamps, model_version, token counts, and ideally latency.
02:38 Priya: current events include request_id, account_id, model, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, start_ts, end_ts, and an approx latency_ms. i'll flag that the field names in the export might be slightly different — we have internal names like 'req_id' and 'tok_in' — sorry for the inconsistencies in the first pass.
03:02 Dr. Omar: is the user_id stored as plain text? for PH compliance we cannot store raw patient identifiers — hashing or PII redaction is required.
03:14 Priya: user_id in logs today is a hashed identifier in our hosted flows — it's a one-way hash using customer-supplied salt if configured. we'll confirm the hashing algorithm and provide sample hashed values.
03:28 Leah: excellent. also retention — our policy is 90 days for full payloads, 1 year for metadata. is that compatible with your log export retention options?
03:40 Jordan: Redwood's default hosted retention is 30 days for request payloads and 365 for metadata unless overridden on Dedicated or Private. for pilots we can extend retention if needed but there are costs and depending on region there are data residency implications.
03:58 Sam: that 30-day default is a blocker for our compliance team. we need the 90-day payload window for investigatory purposes during the pilot.
04:10 Jordan: understood. two options: a) enable extended retention on your hosted tenant for pilot (one-time config + cost delta), or b) run pilot on a Dedicated pool where you can set retention exactly. both are feasible.
04:26 Sam: we prefer hosted if we can get the 90 days temporarily. pricing is less of a blocker for the pilot.
04:33 Priya: we can do temporary extension. i'll document the delta and what fields remain in payload exports.
04:40 Leah: about SOC2 — what artifacts can you share for our auditors?
04:44 Jordan: we can provide the SOC2 Type II report summary, control mappings, and our system architecture diagrams. note: full reports and some evidence require an NDA in some cases. i'll attach the security pack link after the call: https://redwood.example/security-pack (placeholder).
05:05 Sam: we also need evidence of RBAC and admin audit trails. are admin role changes tracked in the audit logs?
05:14 Priya: yes, role changes, API key creates, and console logins are emitted to the audit stream. those are separate from request logs and we can filter by admin events.
05:24 Dr. Omar: small question on redaction — if a prompt includes a patient's name, is there an automatic redaction step prior to persisting logs?
05:35 Priya: not by default. we offer a redact-on-ingest rule set as an opt-in for customers — it can scrub defined fields or run a regex-based PII scrubber. for pilot we can enable a lightweight redaction plugin. note it's not perfect for all languages.
06:00 Leah: can you give an example of the audit log JSON? even a 10-line snippet would help our SIEM mapping.
06:07 Priya: yes, i'll share an example. it might look like {"req_id": "abc123", "model_version": "redwood-v1.2", "user_hash": "...", "latency_ms": 230} — but names may vary.
06:23 Jordan: action item — leah will send a sample of the formats you ingest so priya can map fields.
06:29 Leah: okay i'll zip and upload.
06:33 [00:06:40] Jordan: moving to performance tuning — priya, quick take on batching, kv-cache and whether we've got opportunities to lower token costs.
06:46 Priya: sure — for the current prompt mix we see room for prefix caching and a tuned batch size. the kv cash (sic) hit rate was around 62% on the last run; if we increase TTL for sessions we can get up into the mid-70s which reduces compute by ~12%.
07:04 Dr. Omar: how does ttl interact with privacy — longer ttl means more cached context persisted, correct?
07:12 Priya: correct. longer ttl holds KV cache entries and we treat that as ephemeral memory. for regulated data we recommend not caching sensitive fields, or using per-session ephemeral keys.
07:25 Sam: can we limit caching to non-PII tokens only?
07:29 Priya: not at token granularity today; current tool supports session-level caching control and some attribute-based redaction before caching. it's something on our roadmap to get more fine-grained.
07:44 Leah: back to SSO test — can we schedule it for next tuesday morning? we have two engineers available at 10am PST.
07:51 Jordan: that works for us. priya will be there to help with assertion traces.
07:57 Priya: yes i'll be on the call. jordan, can you invite once we confirm?
08:00 Jordan: will do.
08:04 [00:08:15] Sam: small compliance ask — our auditors want to see the mapping between control IDs and logs; is there a pre-made control map?
08:18 Jordan: we maintain a control mapping doc that ties our audit events to SOC2 control IDs. i'll upload a redline version specific to the pilot.
08:27 Sam: perfect. also we'd like a runbook for how to perform a forensic pull of request payloads for a specific request_id.
08:36 Priya: we have an internal runbook and a CLI tool called the 'evidence export' — i'll share the sanitized runbook; for sensitive exports we require sampling and an approval flow.
08:50 Leah: one more technical — for the SAML assertion we saw an audience mismatch error earlier. is there a place to view the exact SP metadata?
08:58 Priya: yes in the console under integrations -> SSO metadata. sometimes the console UI shows the environment label 'Redhood-hosted' which is a cosmetic typo and has caused confusion. open to digging in live.
09:15 Jordan: noted on the typos, we'll raise an internal jira for console label fixes.
09:21 Dr. Omar: quick question about model_versioning — if we pin to a specific model during pilot, how do we handle automatic fallbacks? we don't want silent fallbacks to lower-quality variants.
09:33 Priya: good call out. by default we have a fallback policy that will attempt to keep availability by switching to a compatible variant; we can enforce strict pinning which will return errors instead. we recommend canary rollouts for version changes.
09:50 Sam: we'd prefer strict pinning for the pilot.
09:53 Priya: noted. we'll set pins.
10:00 [00:10:10] Jordan: OK let's do a quick recap of owners and dates before we wrap.
10:15 Leah: can you also include the cost delta for 90-day retention in the email? we need an internal approval for that spend.
10:23 Jordan: yes, i'll include a clear line item.
10:27 Priya: i'm going to run the benchmark and post the numbers and raw scripts to the shared folder. look for a csv + brief notes.
10:36 Sam: and i'll coordinate with our auditors on the SOC2 checklist and let you know if they need NDA for certain artifacts.
10:43 Jordan: great, thanks. anything else?
10:46 Leah: no, that's it from me.
10:48 Dr. Omar: all good.
10:50 Jordan: thanks everyone, i'll send a meeting note in the next hour with links to the SAML checklist, SOC2 mapping doc, and the action items. talk soon.

End of transcript.

References and links mentioned in meeting: https://redwood.example/security-pack (security pack placeholder), shared drive link (provided after call).

Notes about transcription errors: 'KV cache' transcribed once as 'KV cash', console label 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes misheard as 'Redhood' or 'Red Wood Dedicated'.

Meeting closed 15:42 PST.
